author: Mark Atwood
text:
Section CONFIDENCE CALIBRATION (review-crypto-security pass, 2026-05-14):

ZERO findings filed. crate-jmap-calendars-client is cryptographically inert — a thin JSON-wire-protocol builder over jmap-base-client.

Section-by-section walk:

A (key material lifecycle): No types in this crate hold or derive key material. SessionClient holds JmapClient + Session, both from jmap-base-client (out of scope). The manual Debug impl on SessionClient redacts the inner JmapClient. The session field is Debug-forwarded, but Session's secret-handling discipline lives in jmap-base-client (covered by JMAP-sc1b.99/.104). Nothing to file at this crate's scope.

B (side-channel hygiene): No secret-byte comparisons anywhere. The empty-string guards on State.as_ref() and HashMap creation-id keys check non-secret tokens — JMAP state tokens are opaque cache keys returned in every server response, not secrets. Nothing to file.

C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries): Response parsing is delegated to jmap_base_client::extract_response + serde_json::from_value through #[derive(Deserialize)] on the typed response structs. No slice indexing, no length-prefixed field reads, no .unwrap() on untrusted bytes. All untrusted-input handling that exists is at the HTTP/JSON-parse layer (out of scope) or in jmap-types deserialize impls (out of scope for this client crate). The Id type lacks length validation on Deserialize (Id::new_validated is opt-in; #[derive(Deserialize)] accepts any string), but that is a deliberate types-crate posture, not a calendars-client defect. Nothing to file at this crate's scope.

D (random source quality): No randomness consumed in this crate. Nothing to file.

E (persistent storage of secrets): Per workspace AGENTS.md 'What this workspace builds' and user brief, the kit posture explicitly excludes persistence. This crate writes nothing to disk and holds no long-lived state beyond an in-memory Session value. Nothing to file.

F (logging output safety): No tracing/log/println/eprintln calls in production source (grep confirmed). No types in this crate wrap credentials, tokens, verification codes, or invite codes. The SessionClient.session field forwards Debug to jmap_base_client::Session — Session's own redaction is JMAP-1j9k.99-territory, not this crate's. The workspace Debug-redaction-canary convention applies 'when any new type wraps a credential string'; calendars-client introduces no such type. SessionClient's manual Debug impl claims to redact the JmapClient, but JmapClient is not Debug in the first place, so re-deriving Debug would fail to compile — type system already enforces what a canary would check. Filing a canary here would be defense-in-depth-of-a-tautology, i.e. bikeshedding. Nothing to file.

G (algorithm and parameter choice): No cryptographic primitives invoked. No hashing, signing, AEAD, KDF, MAC, signature scheme, nonce, IV. Confirmed correct posture for a JMAP wire-protocol client crate per user brief. No jmap-cid-types / Sha256 / blob-integrity references appear in this crate (grep confirmed) — blob ids are passed through as opaque jmap_types::Id values, not as hash-typed wire values. Nothing to file.

Sections < 10 minutes: D, E (both vacuous for a wire-protocol client; ~2 minutes each to confirm by grep). These are not 'insufficient' — they are vacuous-by-construction.

Read coverage: I read every .rs file in src/ end-to-end (lib.rs, methods/mod.rs, calendar.rs, event.rs, event_copy.rs, event_notification.rs, event_parse.rs, participant_identity.rs, principal_availability.rs) and tests/helpers.rs in full. I did NOT load the four wiremock smoke-test files (calendar_smoke_tests.rs, event_smoke_tests.rs, event_notification_smoke_tests.rs, participant_identity_smoke_tests.rs, availability_tests.rs) end-to-end — only grepped them for crypto-adjacent keywords (auth/token/cred/secret/invite/signature) and confirmed only 'NoneAuth' (no-credentials test transport) and prose 'authenticated user' / 'auth headers' usage. I did not audit jmap-base-client::extract_response, JmapClient::call internals, ClientError variants (per user brief, out of scope).

Probability I missed a P0: ~5%. Justification: the surface area where a P0 crypto defect could hide in this crate is genuinely tiny — no primitives, no key material, no random, no storage, no logging, all I/O delegated to base-client. The remaining 5% is the chance that (a) a secret somehow leaks via Debug forwarding through SessionClient.session into the consumer's tracing output and the redaction discipline in base-client's Session Debug impl has a gap, OR (b) the unhardened Id Deserialize accepts a malicious oversized id that, when used as a HashMap<Id, _> key in this crate's response types (CalendarEventParseResponse.parsed: HashMap<Id, Vec<CalendarEvent>>, SetResponse.{updated,destroyed,notUpdated,notDestroyed}), enables a memory-DoS in a consumer. Both are upstream concerns and tracked elsewhere (JMAP-1j9k.99/.104 family for Session redaction; Id-validation-on-Deserialize is a known types-crate posture decision). Not raising X > 20% threshold, so no scheduled deeper-pass P1.

If X > 20%: would file a P1 to schedule deeper external crypto review of jmap-base-client::Session redaction + types-crate Id Deserialize hardening as a workspace-level epic. Not filing here because (a) this crate doesn't own either surface, (b) both are tracked in their owning crates' epics, and (c) inflating findings into this epic to fill space is exactly the bikeshedding the workspace rule forbids.

Read-only rule deviations: ZERO. No edits, no writes anywhere, no /tmp files created, no cargo invocations beyond the read-only grep/find/git-log calls in this pass. The pre-existing /tmp/opencode/probe_b.rs from the prior /review-rusty pass was NOT touched (the deviation is documented on the epic from that prior session).
